tasks.corrected_reference_answer: CopyOnWriteArray wraps an indexable array with _copied=False. The first mutation calls _ensure_copied, replacing the wrapped array with np.array(self.array) and setting _copied=True; later writes on that wrapper reuse the copy. Indexed reads return new CopyOnWriteArray wrappers and do not invoke _ensure_copied, but underlying indexing can evaluate data, so this is not a blanket laziness guarantee (xarray/core/indexing.py:786-826).

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The premise is not established by this source. The test demonstrates a factory pattern allowing a custom index to generate extra coordinate variables (xarray/tests/test_indexes.py:761-778). Coordinates.from_xindex calls create_variables once and wraps the result (xarray/core/coordinates.py:363-389). assign_coords shallow-copies the object and updates coordinates (xarray/core/common.py:653-665). Index.create_variables explicitly permits reusing index data or returning existing variables (xarray/core/indexes.py:168-179). Object and mapping construction may cost time, but data materialization, throughput, and any 2-3x comparison require a specific index implementation and measurements.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The test calls a fresh-dataset helper 13 times for each of three attribute scopes, for 39 constructions. This repeats construction of the same small data and coordinate arrays, while keeping mutations isolated (xarray/tests/test_backends.py:5842-5928). Reusing one dataset per scope and clearing all affected attributes between cases could reduce construction work, provided serialization side effects are also reset. Parameterization can make coverage explicit but does not itself reduce construction count. The source supplies no timing evidence that construction is a significant bottleneck relative to netCDF writes.
